guard: a persona definition that would not load back is refused before anything is written (#5404)
why: The suite calls saveAgentFile from ../src, so the refusal it checks is the writer's own.
P1 writes the file without reading it back, so a subscribe entry outside allowSubscribe is saved and every later load of that name fails.
smoke:manager-service-ops checks the same refusal end to end, through define-persona on a real manager that loads core from dist/.
P2 puts the function name and the file path back into the refusal, which an agent then reads as "Couldn't define <name>: saveAgentFile: ... agent file <path>: ...".

mutations.name: P1 the writer saves without reading the file back
mutations.expectRed: saveAgentFile refuses a family wider than every read entry and writes no file
mutations.cell: saveAgentFile refuses a family wider than every read entry and writes no file
mutations.note: A peer could then save a persona that no later load, spawn or redefine can read.

mutations.name: P2 the refusal names the writer and the unwritten file again
mutations.find: throw new Error(`it would not load: ${reason.startsWith(prefix) ? reason.slice(prefix.length) : reason}`);
mutations.replace: throw new Error(`saveAgentFile: "${def.name}" was not saved because it would not load: ${reason}`);
mutations.expectRed: the refusal reads as the rule the file broke
mutations.cell: the refusal reads as the rule the file broke
mutations.note: The agent would see the doubled failure and an internal function name again.
